title: My first game as a solo dev just went live. Would you play it for 10 minutes and tell me what’s wrong with it?
author: Unique_Cranberry5170
selftext:
Hi everyone,

This is my first time shipping a game, so I’m learning everything as I go: building it, getting it through store review, and now the scariest part, letting strangers play it.

The game is Car Dealer Tycoon: Auto Lot. You buy dirty, damaged cars, scrub them clean with your finger, fix and tune them, then haggle with buyers who each have their own budget and patience.

I’d really appreciate it if you could try it and tell me honestly:

* Were the first 10 minutes clear, or did you get lost somewhere?
* Is the haggling fun, or does it get annoying?
* Did anything feel unfair, slow or confusing?
* Any bugs or crashes? (Please mention your phone model.)

It’s free on Google Play: [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.fiveparmak.otogaleri](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.fiveparmak.otogaleri)  
The iOS version is in Apple review.

I’m open to any suggestion, big or small, and I’ll read and reply to every comment. Criticism is exactly what I need right now, so don’t hold back.

Thanks for reading!

comments.author: Lower_Low_4523
comments.body: That looks cool, I’m going to download it

replies.author: Unique_Cranberry5170
replies.body: Thank you! Would love to hear what you think, especially about the haggling. Any feedback helps a lot 🙏

comments.author: WesternShirt1195
comments.body: Just seems like there are a lot of these types of games. So really not interested in trying it

replies.author: Unique_Cranberry5170
replies.body: Fair, the genre is crowded. The part I tried to do differently is the haggling: every buyer has their own budget and patience, and you can serve them tea to keep them at the table. If that’s not your thing, no worries, thanks for taking a look!

comments.author: Three_Tails_Studio
comments.body: What is different about your game from the 500 others that look just like it?

replies.author: Unique_Cranberry5170
replies.body:
Good question. The main differences:

* Cars hide faults (engine, gearbox, electrics) and the price won’t tell you. You need an inspection before buying, so a cheap car can turn out expensive.
* Haggling is a real back-and-forth: buyers have names, budgets and tempers, and they walk away if you push too hard.
* You wash and repair by hand (finger scrubbing, lift repairs), not just a progress bar.
* 33 cities with different demand and rent: pickups sell in Houston, small hatchbacks in Rome.

It’s still a tycoon at heart, but those were the parts I cared about most.

replies.body: Fair enough. Like others have said, change your icon. Its beyond bad and low effort.

replies.body: That’s fair feedback, thanks for being direct. The icon was made with AI help and I can see how it gives that impression. The game itself (the systems, the haggling, the economy) is hand-built, I’ve been working on it for months. I’ll look into a cleaner icon, appreciate it.

comments.author: TheZorro1909
comments.body:
The good:

* no bugs
* game loop made sense
* I liked the inspection mechanics

The bad:

* the music was terrible
* the icon is really generic
* see Screenshot for layout problems
* cleaning a car in one spot cleans the entire car
* I hated it that you are fixed to watch the car move from point to point instead of doing things in the mean time
* the core game loop got quite boring within a few minutes
* I think the art style of the game doesn't match with the menus
